item.research_question: How does the wire electrical discharge machining (WEDM) performance of WNbMoTaZrx (x = 0.5, 1) refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) compare to that of conventional materials?
item.material_system: WNbMoTaZrx (x = 0.5, 1) RHEAs, tungsten, cemented carbide, and industrial pure Zr
item.processing_route: Wire electrical discharge machining (WEDM) with varying electrical parameters
item.test_conditions: Orthogonal and single-factor experiments with different processing parameters
key_findings: 1. The cutting efficiency (CE) of RHEAs is significantly affected by the pulse-on time (ON), pulse-off time (OFF), and peak current (IP).
2. The surface roughness (Ra) of RHEAs is mainly dependent on the ON and IP.
3. The CE of RHEAs can be tuned by optimizing the processing parameters, but it is challenging to tune the surface roughness.
4. The RHEAs maintain the main BCC1 phase enriched with W and Ta elements after WEDM, while the BCC2 phase enriched with Zr and Nb elements disappears.
5. The formation of the upper recast layer consisting of re-solidified particles is the main reason for the relatively larger surface roughness of RHEAs.
item.mechanism: The WEDM process involves the melting and removal of workpiece materials, and the formation of the upper recast layer consisting of re-solidified particles.
item.limitations: The surface roughness of RHEAs is challenging to tune by changing the processing parameters.
item.future_work: Further understanding of the melting and removal mechanisms of RHEAs during WEDM, and the use of advanced WEDM techniques to improve the surface quality.
quotes: The CE of RHEAs can be tuned by optimizing the processing parameters, however, it is challenging to tune the surface roughness of RHEAs by tailoring the processing parameters.
The formation of the upper recast layers, consisting of clusters of particles on the WEDMed surfaces, are the main reasons for the relatively larger surface roughness of the RHEAs.
The high SV can effectively improve the specific discharge energy (SDE), which is beneficial for the melting and throw-out of materials.
